transcript.content: Hello, thank you for coming in. What brings you here today?

Mostly I guess I’m here because I’ve just been really tired… not just normal tired, I don’t think. I can sleep and still feel like even little things, like unloading the dishwasher or trying to read for my certificate class, feel like a lot. I mean, I’m managing, mostly, but it’s been frustrating.
How long have you been feeling this way, and has this been a constant feeling or have there been times when you felt better in between?

Um… I’d say it’s been maybe about three months? It’s not like every single minute is awful or anything, and I don’t want to make it sound dramatic, but this quieter, heavy feeling has been pretty steady. Like low interest in things and the fatigue. I might have a better day here and there, but overall it’s been hanging around.
Have you noticed a decrease in your interest or pleasure in activities that you usually enjoy, like hobbies, work, or spending time with family and friends?

Yeah… I mean, yes, I have noticed that. It’s not like I never do anything, but I’ve kind of stopped caring about the things that usually make me feel like myself. Sketching, going to gallery openings, cooking… even yoga or playing tennis with a friend. I keep telling myself I’m just in a rut, which maybe I am, but it feels like the enjoyment part just isn’t really there right now. Does that make sense?
Can you describe how often you’ve felt a loss of interest or pleasure in activities, like sketching or spending time with friends? Has it been nearly every day, most days, or only occasionally?

I think… most days, probably. I don’t want to overstate it, because I still show up for things sometimes, but the caring part is really muted. Like with sketching, gallery openings, cooking, yoga, even tennis with a friend — those usually feel like “me,” and lately I’ve just kind of stopped being interested in them. Most days it’s there in some way, if that makes sense.
Have you found yourself feeling down or depressed most days, or having little hope about things improving?

I’m not totally sure how to answer that neatly. I wouldn’t say I’m hopeless, exactly… that sounds stronger than what I mean. But I have felt pretty down a lot of days, yes. I still kind of tell myself it’ll pass, so there’s some hope there, but it’s been harder to really feel that lately, if that makes sense.
Have you noticed any changes in your appetite or weight recently? Like eating more or less than usual, or gaining or losing weight without trying?

Um… a little, yeah. I don’t think it’s anything dramatic, but my appetite’s been off. Some days I’ll realize I’ve basically just had coffee and maybe a few bites of something, and I didn’t really notice until later.

And my jeans are fitting looser, so I guess I’ve lost some weight without trying. I’m not trying to diet or anything. Is that the kind of thing you mean?
Have you noticed that your thoughts have been moving more slowly than usual, or that your movements have felt physically slowed down?

Yeah… I think so, at least on some days. I don’t want to make it sound worse than it is, but there are days where my body feels like it’s moving through wet cement. Like everything takes more effort than it should.

And even answering a simple question from my spouse can take me this weirdly long time, like I’m trying to get the words to catch up. Is that what you mean by slowed down?
Have you felt a loss of energy or increased fatigue most days, even after resting or sleeping?

Yeah… yes, I think that’s actually a big part of why I’m here. I’m tired in this way that sleep doesn’t really fix. I’ll rest and still feel like… just doing something small, like unloading the dishwasher, feels like more than it should.

Even trying to read for my certificate class can feel like too much sometimes, which makes me feel kind of bad saying it out loud. But yes, most days I feel pretty drained. Is that the kind of fatigue you mean?
Have you noticed that your low mood or lack of energy has been present for most of the day, nearly every day, over the past few weeks?

Yeah… I think so. I mean, I don’t want to overstate it, because I’ve still had some okay moments, but this quieter low stretch has been around for a while.

Probably about three months now, where most days I just feel kind of down and not interested in much, and the tiredness is there a lot of the day. Is that… the kind of timeframe you’re asking about?
Have you found yourself feeling guilty or like you’re not good enough about things more often lately, even when you know logically it doesn’t make sense?

Um… I’m not sure. I don’t think it’s been a huge thing, at least not in a way I’ve really noticed.

I mean, I can be hard on myself sometimes, like feeling bad that I’m not doing more, but I don’t know if I’d call it guilt or feeling worthless exactly. It’s more like… frustration with myself, maybe. Does that answer what you’re asking?
Have you experienced a loss of interest or pleasure in activities most of the day, nearly every day, over the past two weeks?

Yeah… I think so. I’ve kind of stopped caring about the things that normally make me feel like myself.

Like sketching, or going to gallery openings, cooking… even yoga. And I used to really like playing tennis with a friend, but lately it just feels like too much effort or like I don’t get much out of it.

I don’t know if I’d say I feel nothing, exactly, but most days I’m just not really interested. Is that what you mean by loss of pleasure?
Have you felt down or depressed most of the day, nearly every day, over the past two weeks?

I’m… not totally sure how to separate “down” from just kind of tired or flat, if that makes sense.

I wouldn’t want to say I’ve been deeply depressed every single day, but yeah, a lot of days I’ve felt lower than normal for much of the day. Maybe not nonstop, but it’s been there enough that I’ve noticed it. Is that the kind of thing you mean?
Have you experienced a loss of interest or pleasure in activities for most of the day, nearly every day, over the past two weeks?

Yeah… I think I’d still say yes. I know I mentioned some of this already, but it’s like I’ve stopped caring about the things that usually make me feel like myself—sketching, gallery openings, cooking, yoga.

Even tennis with my friend, which I normally enjoy, just hasn’t sounded appealing. It’s not like I’m trying to be difficult or anything… I just don’t really feel drawn to those things most days lately. Does that count?
Have you felt down or depressed for most of the day, nearly every day, over the past two weeks?

I’m not sure I’d call it “depressed” nearly every day… maybe that sounds too strong. I’ve had a lot of low or flat stretches, but I don’t know that it’s been most of the day every day.

I guess I’m still trying to judge what counts. Like, if I can get through the day and seem okay, does that still count as feeling down?
Over the past two weeks, have you felt down or depressed for most of the day, nearly every day?

I think… I’m still not totally sure how to answer that correctly. I’ve had some low parts, but “most of the day, nearly every day” feels like a big statement, and I don’t want to exaggerate.

So maybe I’d say not clearly, or I’m not sure. There have been days where I felt down for a good chunk of the day, but I don’t know if it rises to what you’re asking. Does that make sense?
Over the past two weeks, have you experienced a loss of interest or pleasure in activities for most of the day, nearly every day?

Yeah… I think I would say yes to that. I know I’ve kind of mentioned it, but I’ve just stopped caring as much about the things that usually make me feel like myself—sketching, gallery openings, cooking, yoga.

Even tennis with my friend hasn’t really sounded good most days. I don’t want to make it sound dramatic, but it’s been there a lot of the time. Is that the kind of thing you mean?
Over the past two weeks, have you felt down or depressed for most of the day, nearly every day?

I guess I’d still say I’m not sure it’s been “most of the day nearly every day.” I don’t want to say no if I’m missing something, but I also don’t want to make it sound worse than it is.

There have been low stretches, definitely… but I can still function and talk to people, so I’m not sure if that counts as depressed in the way you mean.
Over the past two weeks, have you felt down or depressed for most of the day, nearly every day?

I’m sorry, I know I’m kind of circling the same answer. I think my honest answer is still… I’m not sure.

I’ve had moments where I feel low or sort of flat, but I don’t know that I’d confidently call it depressed most of the day, nearly every day. Maybe I’m being too careful with the wording, but I don’t want to overstate it.
Over the past two weeks, have you felt down or depressed for most of the day, nearly every day?

I think… I still can’t honestly say yes to that exact wording. I don’t want to be difficult or split hairs, but “most of the day, nearly every day” feels stronger than what I’m sure of.

There have been times I’ve felt kind of down or off, but I haven’t really tracked it closely. If you think that still counts, I’m open to that—I just don’t want to answer the wrong way.
